```{r BIOREGIONALIZATION THIESSEN MAP}
# ==============================================================================
# STANDALONE DELDIR BIOREGIONALIZATION MAP CREATION - TWO VERSIONS
# ==============================================================================

   # Transform to projected coordinate system for accurate calculations
       results_sf_proj <- sf::st_transform(results_sf, crs = 32638)  # UTM Zone 38N
       georgia_boundary_proj <- sf::st_transform(Georgia_Boundary, crs = 32638)
   
   # Extract coordinates and site information
       coords_proj <- sf::st_coordinates(results_sf_proj)
       site_coords_df <- data.frame(
           x = coords_proj[, "X"],
           y = coords_proj[, "Y"],
           site_id = results_summary$site_id,
           bioregion = results_summary$bioregion,
           species_richness = results_summary$species_richness
       )
   
   # Get Georgia boundary box for Thiessen polygon creation
       georgia_bbox_proj <- sf::st_bbox(georgia_boundary_proj)
   
   # Create Thiessen polygons using deldir
       thiessen_deldir <- deldir::deldir(
           x = site_coords_df$x,
           y = site_coords_df$y,
           rw = c(georgia_bbox_proj$xmin, georgia_bbox_proj$xmax, 
                  georgia_bbox_proj$ymin, georgia_bbox_proj$ymax),
           suppressMsge = TRUE
       )
   
   # Convert deldir tiles to sf polygons
       thiessen_tiles <- deldir::tile.list(thiessen_deldir)
       
       tile_to_polygon <- function(tile) {
           if (length(tile$x) < 3) return(NULL)
           
           coords_matrix <- matrix(c(c(tile$x, tile$x[1]), 
                                   c(tile$y, tile$y[1])), ncol = 2)
           poly <- sf::st_polygon(list(coords_matrix))
           return(poly)
       }
       
       polygon_list <- purrr::map(thiessen_tiles, tile_to_polygon) %>%
           purrr::compact()
       
       thiessen_sf <- sf::st_sf(
           tile_id = 1:length(polygon_list),
           geometry = sf::st_sfc(polygon_list, crs = 32638)
       )
   
   # Add bioregion information
       thiessen_with_bioregions <- thiessen_sf %>%
           dplyr::mutate(
               site_id = site_coords_df$site_id,
               bioregion = site_coords_df$bioregion,
               species_richness = site_coords_df$species_richness
           )
   
   # Clip to Georgia boundary
       thiessen_clipped <- sf::st_intersection(thiessen_with_bioregions, georgia_boundary_proj)
   
   # Dissolve polygons by bioregion
       bioregion_polygons_proj <- thiessen_clipped %>%
           dplyr::group_by(bioregion) %>%
           dplyr::summarise(
               n_polygons = dplyr::n(),
               .groups = 'drop'
           )
   
   # Transform back to WGS84
       bioregion_polygons <- sf::st_transform(bioregion_polygons_proj, crs = 4326)
       thiessen_clipped_wgs84 <- sf::st_transform(thiessen_clipped, crs = 4326)
   
   # VERSION 1: Clean dissolved regions map
       bioregion_map_clean <- ggplot() +
           geom_sf(
               data = bioregion_polygons,
               aes(fill = factor(bioregion)),
               alpha = 0.8,
               color = "white",
               linewidth = 1.5
           ) +
           geom_sf(
               data = Georgia_Boundary,
               fill = NA,
               color = "black",
               linewidth = 2
           ) +
           geom_sf(
               data = results_sf,
               aes(size = species_richness),
               color = "black",
               alpha = 0.9
           ) +
           scale_fill_viridis_d(
               name = "Bioregion",
               option = "turbo",
               begin = 0.1,
               end = 0.9,
               guide = "none"
           ) +
           scale_size_continuous(
               name = "Species Richness",
               range = c(1, 4),
               guide = "none"
           ) +
           theme_void() +
           theme(
               panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
               plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)#,
               #plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
           )
   
   # VERSION 2: Map with Thiessen polygon boundaries visible
       
        jenks_breaks <- classIntervals(
            results_sf$species_richness,
            n = 3,
            style = "jenks"
        )
        
        # Create a factor variable with Jenks break categories
          results_sf <- results_sf |>
              dplyr::mutate(
                  richness_class = cut(
                      species_richness,
                      breaks = jenks_breaks$brks,
                      include.lowest = TRUE,
                      labels = FALSE
                  )
              )

          bioregion_map_thiessen <- ggplot() +
              geom_sf(
                  data = thiessen_clipped_wgs84,
                  aes(fill = factor(bioregion)),
                  alpha = 0.7,
                  color = "white",
                  linewidth = 0.3
              ) +
              geom_sf(
                  data = bioregion_polygons,
                  fill = NA,
                  color = "black",
                  linewidth = 1.5
              ) +
              geom_sf(
                  data = Georgia_Boundary,
                  fill = NA,
                  color = "black",
                  linewidth = 2
              ) +
              geom_sf(
                  data = results_sf,
                  aes(size = factor(richness_class)),
                  color = "black",
                  alpha = 0.9
              ) +
              scale_fill_viridis_d(
                  name = "Bioregion",
                  option = "turbo",
                  begin = 0.1,
                  end = 0.9,
                  guide = "none"
              ) +
              scale_size_manual(
                  name = "Species Richness",
                  values = c(2, 4.5, 7),
                  guide = "none"
              ) +
              theme_void() +
              theme(
                  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
                  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
              )
   
   # Create standalone legend for bioregions
       legend_bioregion <- ggplot() +
           geom_sf(
               data = bioregion_polygons,
               aes(fill = factor(bioregion)),
               alpha = 0.8

                   title.hjust = 0.5,

               )
           )
   
   # Create standalone legend for species richness
       legend_richness <- ggplot() +
           geom_sf(
               data = results_sf,

           ) +

               name = "Species Richness",

           ) +
           theme_void() +
           theme(
               legend.position = "bottom",
               legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
               legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
               panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
               plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
           ) +
           guides(
               size = guide_legend(
                   title.position = "top",
                   title.hjust = 0.5,
                   override.aes = list(alpha = 1)
               )
           )
   
   # Display both maps
       print(bioregion_map_clean)
       print(bioregion_map_thiessen)
```

```{r RAREFACTION}
  # --- RAREFACTION & ESTIMATORS ---
  
    # Retrieve site-species matrix
      site_species_matrix <- site_species_final
    
    # Inspect dimensions and column names
      cat("Matrix dimensions:", dim(site_species_matrix), "\n")
      cat("Species columns:\n")
      print(colnames(site_species_matrix))
    
    # Ensure matrix is in proper format
      site_species_matrix <- as.data.frame(site_species_matrix)
    
    # Calculate Chao1 and Jackknife Estimators
      chao1_estimate <- estimateR(t(site_species_matrix))
      jack1_estimate <- specpool(site_species_matrix, pool = rep("all", nrow(site_species_matrix)))
    
    # Compute mean Chao1 estimate
      mean_chao1 <- mean(chao1_estimate["S.chao1", ], na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Prepare incidence data for iNEXT (single assemblage)
      inext_input <- c(nrow(site_species_matrix), colSums(site_species_matrix))
      inext_input <- inext_input[inext_input > 0]  # remove species never observed
      inext_result <- iNEXT(inext_input, q = 0, datatype = "incidence_freq")
    
    # Plot accumulation curve and overlay estimates
      specacc <- specaccum(site_species_matrix, method = "random")
    
    # Plot accumulation
      plot(specacc, ci.type = "polygon", col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, ci.lty = 0, ci.col = "lightgreen")
      legend("bottomright", legend = c("Accumulation", "Chao1", "Jackknife1"), col = c("darkgreen", "blue", "purple"), pch = c(NA, 16, 17), lty = c(1, NA, NA))
    
    # Plot iNEXT (single assemblage)
      print(
        ggiNEXT(inext_result, type = 1) +
          theme_minimal() +
          ggtitle("iNEXT Species Accumulation Curve")
      )
    
    # Output estimates
      list(
        Chao1 = chao1_estimate,
        Jackknife1 = jack1_estimate,
        iNEXT_summary = inext_result$AsyEst
      )
```

CHUNK 17. NETWORK ANALYSIS

```{r NETWORK ANALYSIS}

# ==============================================================================
# VEECH CO-OCCURRENCE NETWORK
# ==============================================================================

    # Transpose and format for cooccur
        cooc_input <- t(site_species_matrix)
    
    # Assign cleaned species names
        rownames(cooc_input) <- gsub("_", " ", rownames(cooc_input))
    
    # Run cooccur analysis
        co <- cooccur(mat = cooc_input, spp_names = TRUE)
        co_table <- as.data.frame(print(co))
    
    # Define nodes for Veech network
        veech_nodes <- data.frame(
            id = 1:nrow(cooc_input),
            label = rownames(cooc_input),
            color = "grey",
            shadow = TRUE
        )
    
    # Define edges for Veech network
        veech_edges <- data.frame(
            from = co_table$sp1,
            to = co_table$sp2,
            width = 1,
            color = ifelse(
                co_table$p_lt <= 0.05, "red",          # Red = significant negative association
                ifelse(co_table$p_gt <= 0.05, "blue", "green")  # Blue = significant positive, Green = neutral
            )
        )
    
    # Visualize Veech network
        veech_network <- visNetwork(nodes = veech_nodes, edges = veech_edges) %>%
            visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_kk") %>%
            visNodes(size = 15) %>%
            visEdges(arrows = "none") %>%
            visOptions(highlightNearest = TRUE)
    
    # Display Veech network
        print(veech_network)


# ==============================================================================
# COUNT CO-OCCURRENCE NETWORK ANALYSIS
# ==============================================================================
        
    # Ensure binary matrix (presence/absence)
        site_species_binary <- site_species_final
        site_species_binary[site_species_binary > 1] <- 1
    
    # Clean species names for display
        colnames(site_species_binary) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(site_species_binary))
    
    # Calculate co-occurrence counts between all species pairs
        cooccur_counts <- site_species_binary %>%
            as.matrix() %>%
            t() %>%                                     # Transpose to species × sites
            tcrossprod()                                # Matrix multiplication gives co-occurrence counts
        
    # Set diagonal to 0 (species don't co-occur with themselves for edge purposes)
        diag(cooccur_counts) <- 0
    
    # Calculate site occurrence counts for each species (node sizes)
        site_counts <- colSums(site_species_binary)
    
    # Create adjacency matrix for network (only keep edges with co-occurrence > threshold)
        cooccur_threshold <- 1                          # Minimum co-occurrences to show edge
        adj_matrix <- cooccur_counts
        adj_matrix[adj_matrix < cooccur_threshold] <- 0
    
    # Create igraph object
        cooccur_graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
            adj_matrix, 
            mode = "undirected", 
            weighted = TRUE, 
            diag = FALSE
        )

    # Function to extract genus and species for sorting
        extract_genus_species <- function(species_names) {
            parsed <- stringr::str_split(species_names, " ", simplify = TRUE)
            data.frame(
                full_name = species_names,
                genus = parsed[, 1],
                species = parsed[, 2],
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE
            )
        }

    # Create alphabetical ordering
        species_df <- extract_genus_species(names(site_counts))
        alphabetical_order <- species_df %>%
            dplyr::arrange(genus, species) %>%
            dplyr::pull(full_name)

    # Create optimal layout function
        create_optimal_layout <- function(species_order, radius = 2.5) {
            n_nodes <- length(species_order)
            order_indices <- match(species_order, V(cooccur_graph)$name)
            
            angles <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = n_nodes + 1)[1:n_nodes]
            
            layout_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = vcount(cooccur_graph), ncol = 2)
            layout_matrix[order_indices, 1] <- radius * cos(angles)
            layout_matrix[order_indices, 2] <- radius * sin(angles)
            
            return(layout_matrix)
        }

    # Create layout
        optimal_alpha_layout <- create_optimal_layout(alphabetical_order, radius = 2.5)

    # Set vertex attributes
        V(cooccur_graph)$name <- names(site_counts)
        V(cooccur_graph)$site_count <- site_counts[V(cooccur_graph)$name]
        V(cooccur_graph)$size <- scales::rescale(site_counts[V(cooccur_graph)$name], to = c(6, 20))
        V(cooccur_graph)$label.cex <- 0.7
        V(cooccur_graph)$label.color <- "black"
        V(cooccur_graph)$frame.color <- "white"
        V(cooccur_graph)$frame.width <- 1.5

    # Set edge attributes
        edge_weights <- E(cooccur_graph)$weight
        E(cooccur_graph)$weight_original <- edge_weights
        E(cooccur_graph)$width <- scales::rescale(edge_weights, to = c(1.5, 8))

    # Create plotting function with no title
        create_subtle_green_plot <- function(layout_matrix, species_order) {
            # Simpler green scheme
                V(cooccur_graph)$color <- colorRampPalette(c("#9cdf8d", "#3541A5"))(max(site_counts))[site_counts[V(cooccur_graph)$name]]
                E(cooccur_graph)$color <- scales::alpha(colorRampPalette(c("#9cdf8d", "#3541A5"))(max(edge_weights))[edge_weights], 0.6)
            
            label_angles <- atan2(layout_matrix[, 2], layout_matrix[, 1])
            label_degrees <- label_angles * 180 / pi
            adjusted_angles <- ifelse(abs(label_degrees) > 90, label_degrees + 180, label_degrees)
            
            par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5))            # Removed title margin
            
            plot(cooccur_graph,
                 layout = layout_matrix,
                 vertex.label = V(cooccur_graph)$name,
                 vertex.label.dist = 0.8,
                 vertex.label.degree = adjusted_angles * pi / 180,
                 vertex.label.cex = 0.7,
                 edge.curved = 0.2,
                 main = "",                              # No title
                 rescale = FALSE,
                 xlim = c(-3.2, 3.2),
                 ylim = c(-3.2, 3.2),
                 asp = 1)
        }

    # Create the circular network plot
        create_subtle_green_plot(optimal_alpha_layout, alphabetical_order)



# ==============================================================================
# NETWORK ANALYSIS STATISTICS EXTRACTION
# ==============================================================================
    # Use objects already created above
        cooccur_matrix <- cooccur_counts
        veech_table <- co_table
        # site_counts already exists from earlier section
    
    # --- CO-OCCURRENCE MATRIX STATISTICS ---
        # Extract upper triangle of matrix (avoid double counting pairs)
            upper_tri_indices <- upper.tri(cooccur_matrix)
            cooccur_values <- cooccur_matrix[upper_tri_indices]
        
        # Remove zero values for meaningful statistics
            nonzero_cooccur <- cooccur_values[cooccur_values > 0]
        
        # Calculate summary statistics
            cooccur_stats <- list(
                total_pairs = length(cooccur_values),
                pairs_with_cooccurrence = length(nonzero_cooccur),
                mean_cooccurrence = round(mean(nonzero_cooccur), 2),
                median_cooccurrence = round(median(nonzero_cooccur), 2),
                min_cooccurrence = min(nonzero_cooccur),
                max_cooccurrence = max(nonzero_cooccur),
                range_cooccurrence = paste(min(nonzero_cooccur), "-", max(nonzero_cooccur))
            )
    
    # --- IDENTIFY TOP CO-OCCURRING SPECIES PAIRS ---
        # Create data frame of all species pairs with their co-occurrence counts
            species_names <- rownames(cooccur_matrix)
            pair_data <- expand.grid(
                species1 = species_names,
                species2 = species_names,
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE
            ) |>
                dplyr::filter(species1 < species2) |>
                dplyr::mutate(
                    cooccur_count = purrr::map2_dbl(species1, species2, ~ {
                        cooccur_matrix[.x, .y]
                    })
                ) |>
                dplyr::arrange(desc(cooccur_count))
        
        # Top co-occurring pairs
            top_pairs <- pair_data |>
                dplyr::slice_head(n = 2) |>
                dplyr::mutate(
                    pair_name = paste(species1, "and", species2),
                    formatted_result = paste0(pair_name, " (n = ", cooccur_count, " sites)")
                )
    
    # --- IDENTIFY LEAST CO-OCCURRING SPECIES ---
        # Calculate total co-occurrences per species (excluding self)
            species_cooccur_totals <- purrr::map_dbl(species_names, ~ {
                species_row <- cooccur_matrix[.x, ]
                species_col <- cooccur_matrix[, .x]
                sum(species_row) + sum(species_col) - cooccur_matrix[.x, .x]
            }) |>
                purrr::set_names(species_names)
        
        # Identify species with lowest co-occurrence
            least_cooccurring <- species_cooccur_totals |>
                sort() |>
                head(3)
    
    # --- VEECH POSITIVE ASSOCIATIONS ---
        # Extract significantly positive associations (p_gt <= 0.05)
            positive_associations <- veech_table |>
                dplyr::filter(p_gt <= 0.05) |>
                dplyr::arrange(p_gt) |>
                dplyr::mutate(
                    species_pair = paste(sp1_name, "and", sp2_name),
                    p_value_formatted = paste0("p = ", round(p_gt, 4))
                )
        
        # Count and format positive associations
            n_positive_pairs <- nrow(positive_associations)
            positive_pairs_text <- if (n_positive_pairs > 0) {
                positive_associations |>
                    dplyr::slice_head(n = 3) |>
                    dplyr::pull(species_pair) |>
                    paste(collapse = ", ")
            } else {
                "No significant positive associations detected"
            }
    
    # --- COMPILE RESULTS SUMMARY ---
        network_analysis_summary <- list(
            cooccurrence_statistics = cooccur_stats,
            top_cooccurring_pairs = top_pairs,
            least_cooccurring_species = least_cooccurring,
            positive_associations = list(
                count = n_positive_pairs,
                pairs = positive_pairs_text,
                full_table = positive_associations
            ),
            species_site_counts = site_counts
        )
    
    # Export to global environment
        assign("network_analysis_summary", network_analysis_summary, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    
    # --- EXPORT COMPLETE ANALYSIS ---
        assign("complete_cooccurrence_analysis", list(
            circular_graph = cooccur_graph,
            circular_layout = optimal_alpha_layout,
            alphabetical_order = alphabetical_order,
            veech_analysis = co,
            veech_table = co_table,
            veech_network = veech_network,
            site_counts = site_counts,
            cooccur_matrix = cooccur_counts
        ), envir = .GlobalEnv)
    
    # --- PRINT KEY RESULTS FOR MANUSCRIPT ---
        cat("=== COMPLETE CO-OCCURRENCE ANALYSIS FINISHED ===\n\n")
        cat("Circular network: Clean plot with no title\n")
        cat("Veech network: Interactive statistical co-occurrence analysis\n\n")
        
        cat("=== NETWORK ANALYSIS SUMMARY ===\n\n")
        cat("Co-occurrence Statistics:\n")
        cat("  Mean co-occurrence:", cooccur_stats$mean_cooccurrence, "sites\n")
        cat("  Median co-occurrence:", cooccur_stats$median_cooccurrence, "sites\n")
        cat("  Range:", cooccur_stats$range_cooccurrence, "sites\n")
        cat("  Total species pairs with co-occurrence:", cooccur_stats$pairs_with_cooccurrence, "\n\n")
        
        cat("Top Co-occurring Species Pairs:\n")
        purrr::walk(top_pairs$formatted_result, ~ cat("  ", .x, "\n"))
        cat("\n")
        
        cat("Least Co-occurring Species:\n")
        purrr::iwalk(least_cooccurring, ~ cat("  ", .y, ": ", .x, " total co-occurrences\n"))
        cat("\n")
        
        cat("Veech Positive Associations:\n")
        cat("  Number of significant positive pairs:", n_positive_pairs, "\n")
        if (n_positive_pairs > 0) {
            cat("  Most significant pairs:", positive_pairs_text, "\n")
        }  
```

```{r NETWORK HEATMAP}
  # Assume cooccur_counts is your matrix, and colnames/rownames are cleaned
    mat <- cooccur_counts

    cooccur_long <- as.data.frame(mat) %>%
```

```{r DISTRIBUTION OVERLAP ANALYSES}

  # Set output directory
  output_dir <- "specify your directory here"

  
  # Define the modeled species
    target_species <- names(successful_ensemble_results)
  
  # Build species code / full name lookup from inherited name_mapping
      species_names <- as.list(setNames(
          gsub("_", " ", names(name_mapping[name_mapping %in% target_species])),
          name_mapping[name_mapping %in% target_species]
      ))

# =============================================================================
# 1A. CONTINUOUS NICHE OVERLAP ANALYSIS
# =============================================================================

  # Extract continuous prediction rasters for ensemble models
    ensemble_rasters <- map(target_species, function(sp) {
        raster_obj <- successful_ensemble_results[[sp]]$ensemble_predictions
        names(raster_obj) <- sp
        return(raster_obj)
    })
    names(ensemble_rasters) <- target_species

  # Retrieve per-species maxTSS thresholds from chunk 13
    species_thresholds <- map_dbl(target_species, function(sp) {
        get(paste0(sp, "_ensemble_threshold"))
    })
    names(species_thresholds) <- target_species

  # Calculate pairwise niche overlap on continuous surfaces
    continuous_overlap_results <- map_dfr(target_species, function(sp1) {
        map_dfr(target_species, function(sp2) {
            if (sp1 != sp2) {
                raster1 <- ensemble_rasters[[sp1]]
                raster2 <- ensemble_rasters[[sp2]]
                
                warren_i   <- nicheOverlap(raster1, raster2, stat = 'I')
                schoener_d <- nicheOverlap(raster1, raster2, stat = 'D')
                correlation <- cor(values(raster1), values(raster2), use = "complete.obs")
                rank_corr   <- cor(values(raster1), values(raster2), 
                                   method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
                
                tibble(
                    Species1             = sp1,
                    Species2             = sp2,
                    Species1_Full        = species_names[[sp1]],
                    Species2_Full        = species_names[[sp2]],
                    Warrens_I            = round(warren_i, 3),
                    Schoeners_D          = round(schoener_d, 3),
                    Pearson_Correlation   = round(correlation, 3),
                    Spearman_Correlation  = round(rank_corr, 3)
                )
            }
        }) %>%
            filter(!is.null(.))
    })

# =============================================================================
# 1B. BINARY (maxTSS-THRESHOLDED) NICHE OVERLAP ANALYSIS
# =============================================================================

  # Create binary prediction rasters using per-species maxTSS thresholds
    binary_rasters <- map(target_species, function(sp) {
        continuous  <- ensemble_rasters[[sp]]
        threshold   <- species_thresholds[[sp]]
        binary_rast <- continuous >= threshold
        names(binary_rast) <- sp
        return(binary_rast)
    })
    names(binary_rasters) <- target_species

  # Summarize predicted range size per species
    cell_area_km2 <- prod(res(ensemble_rasters[[1]])) * (111^2)
    georgia_total_cells <- sum(!is.na(values(ensemble_rasters[[1]])))
    georgia_area_km2 <- georgia_total_cells * cell_area_km2

    range_size_summary <- map_dfr(target_species, function(sp) {
        n_suitable <- sum(values(binary_rasters[[sp]]) == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
        tibble(
            Species_Code    = sp,
            Species_Name    = species_names[[sp]],
            MaxTSS_Threshold = round(species_thresholds[[sp]], 3),
            Suitable_Cells  = n_suitable,
            Range_km2       = round(n_suitable * cell_area_km2, 1),
            Pct_Georgia     = round(100 * n_suitable / georgia_total_cells, 1)
        )
    })

  # Calculate pairwise overlap on binary surfaces
    binary_overlap_results <- map_dfr(target_species, function(sp1) {
        map_dfr(target_species, function(sp2) {
            if (sp1 != sp2) {
                raster1 <- binary_rasters[[sp1]]
                raster2 <- binary_rasters[[sp2]]
                
                # Standard overlap metrics on binary surfaces
                  warren_i   <- nicheOverlap(raster1, raster2, stat = 'I')
                  schoener_d <- nicheOverlap(raster1, raster2, stat = 'D')
                  correlation <- cor(values(raster1), values(raster2), use = "complete.obs")
                  rank_corr   <- cor(values(raster1), values(raster2), 
                                     method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
                
                tibble(
                    Species1             = sp1,
                    Species2             = sp2,
                    Species1_Full        = species_names[[sp1]],
                    Species2_Full        = species_names[[sp2]],
                    Warrens_I            = round(warren_i, 3),
                    Schoeners_D          = round(schoener_d, 3),
                    Pearson_Correlation   = round(correlation, 3),
                    Spearman_Correlation  = round(rank_corr, 3)
                )
            }
        }) %>%
            filter(!is.null(.))
    })

# =============================================================================
# 1C. RANGE OVERLAP METRICS (JACCARD & SØRENSEN) ON BINARY SURFACES
# =============================================================================

    range_overlap_results <- map_dfr(target_species, function(sp1) {
        map_dfr(target_species, function(sp2) {
            if (sp1 != sp2) {
                vals1 <- values(binary_rasters[[sp1]])
                vals2 <- values(binary_rasters[[sp2]])
                
                # Remove cells where either raster is NA
                  valid       <- !is.na(vals1) & !is.na(vals2)
                  v1          <- vals1[valid]
                  v2          <- vals2[valid]
                
                # Set operations on predicted presence cells
                  n_sp1       <- sum(v1 == 1)
                  n_sp2       <- sum(v2 == 1)
                  n_intersect <- sum(v1 == 1 & v2 == 1)
                  n_union     <- sum(v1 == 1 | v2 == 1)
                
                # Jaccard index: intersection / union
                  jaccard  <- ifelse(n_union > 0, n_intersect / n_union, NA_real_)
                
                # Sørensen coefficient: 2 * intersection / (A + B)
                  sorensen <- ifelse((n_sp1 + n_sp2) > 0, 
                                     2 * n_intersect / (n_sp1 + n_sp2), NA_real_)
                
                # Proportion of each species' range overlapping with the other
                  prop_sp1_shared <- ifelse(n_sp1 > 0, n_intersect / n_sp1, NA_real_)
                  prop_sp2_shared <- ifelse(n_sp2 > 0, n_intersect / n_sp2, NA_real_)
                
                tibble(
                    Species1           = sp1,
                    Species2           = sp2,
                    Species1_Full      = species_names[[sp1]],
                    Species2_Full      = species_names[[sp2]],
                    Intersection_cells = n_intersect,
                    Union_cells        = n_union,
                    Jaccard            = round(jaccard, 3),
                    Sorensen           = round(sorensen, 3),
                    Prop_Sp1_Shared    = round(prop_sp1_shared, 3),
                    Prop_Sp2_Shared    = round(prop_sp2_shared, 3)
                )
            }
        }) %>%
            filter(!is.null(.))
    })

  # Create symmetric matrices for visualization
      create_overlap_matrix <- function(overlap_data, metric) {
          overlap_matrix <- matrix(1.0,
                                   nrow = length(target_species),
                                   ncol = length(target_species),
                                   dimnames = list(target_species, target_species))
  
          walk(seq_len(nrow(overlap_data)), function(i) {
              sp1   <- overlap_data$Species1[i]
              sp2   <- overlap_data$Species2[i]
              value <- overlap_data[[metric]][i]
              overlap_matrix[sp1, sp2] <<- value
              overlap_matrix[sp2, sp1] <<- value
          })
  
          return(overlap_matrix)
      }

  # Continuous overlap matrices

# =============================================================================
# 4. VISUALIZE RANGE OVERLAP — JACCARD & SØRENSEN
# =============================================================================

    png(file.path(output_dir, "range_overlap_matrices.png"), 
        width = 16, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
    
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 2))
  
    corrplot(jaccard_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper",

  # Extract variable importance for all species

  # Create importance matrix
    importance_wide <- importance_comparison |>
        dplyr::select(species, var, rel.inf) |>
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = rel.inf, values_fill = 0) |>
        tibble::column_to_rownames("var")
  
  # Create heatmap of variable importance
    importance_heatmap <- importance_wide %>%
        rownames_to_column("Variable") %>%
        pivot_longer(-Variable, names_to = "Species", values_to = "Importance") %>%
        ggplot(aes(x = Species, y = Variable, fill = Importance)) +
        geom_tile() +
        scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Relative\nImportance (%)") +
        labs(
            title = "Variable Importance Comparison Across Species",
            x = "Species", y = "Environmental Variables"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)
        )
  
  ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "variable_importance_heatmap.png"),
         importance_heatmap, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)

# =============================================================================
# 6. PREDICTION CORRELATION ANALYSIS
# =============================================================================

  # Extract values from all prediction rasters
    prediction_values <- map_dfc(target_species, function(sp) {
        raster_obj <- successful_ensemble_results[[sp]]$ensemble_predictions
        values_vec <- values(raster_obj)

  # Calculate correlation matrix

             mar = c(0,0,2,0))

# =============================================================================

  # Comprehensive comparison table: continuous and binary overlap per species
    comparison_summary <- tibble(

  # Prepare complete matrix data for continuous surfaces
    build_matrix_data <- function(overlap_data, metrics) {
        map_dfr(target_species, function(sp1) {
            map_dfr(target_species, function(sp2) {
                if (sp1 == sp2) {
                    row <- tibble(Species1 = sp1, Species2 = sp2)
                    walk(metrics, ~ { row[[.x]] <<- 1.0 })
                    return(row)
                } else {
                    pair_data <- overlap_data %>%
                        filter((Species1 == sp1 & Species2 == sp2) | 
                               (Species1 == sp2 & Species2 == sp1))
                    if (nrow(pair_data) > 0) {
                        row <- tibble(Species1 = sp1, Species2 = sp2)
                        walk(metrics, ~ { row[[.x]] <<- pair_data[[.x]][1] })
                        return(row)
                    }
                }
            })
        }) %>%
            filter(!is.na(Species1))
    }

    continuous_matrix_data <- build_matrix_data(
        continuous_overlap_results, 
        c("Warrens_I", "Schoeners_D", "Pearson_Correlation", "Spearman_Correlation")
    )

        binary_overlap_results,
        c("Warrens_I", "Schoeners_D", "Pearson_Correlation", "Spearman_Correlation")
    )
    
    range_matrix_data <- build_matrix_data(
        range_overlap_results,
        c("Jaccard", "Sorensen")
    )

  # Function to create matrix plot with values
    create_matrix_plot <- function(data, metric_col, title, colors, limits = c(0, 1)) {
        ggplot(data, aes(x = Species1, y = Species2, fill = !!sym(metric_col))) +
            geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
            geom_text(aes(label = round(!!sym(metric_col), 3)), 
                     color = "white", size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
            scale_fill_gradientn(
                colors = colors,
                name = "",
                limits = limits,
                breaks = seq(limits[1], limits[2], length.out = 5)
            ) +
            labs(title = title) +
            theme_minimal() +
            theme(
                axis.title = element_blank(),
                axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
                axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
                panel.grid = element_blank(),
                plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
                legend.position = "right",
                legend.key.height = unit(1, "cm"),
                legend.key.width = unit(0.5, "cm"),
                panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
                plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
            ) +
            coord_fixed()
    }

  # Continuous surface ggplot matrices
    cont_warrens_plot  <- create_matrix_plot(continuous_matrix_data, "Warrens_I",

  # Range overlap ggplot matrices
```
