-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 CHUNK 20. SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS}
# ==============================================================================
# BIOREGIONALIZATION AND CO-OCCURRENCE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
# ==============================================================================

    # Retrieve core objects from the primary analysis
        clustgeo_results    <- get("clustgeo_bioregionalization")
        reference_clusters  <- clustgeo_results$clustering$bioregions
        site_species_ref    <- clustgeo_results$bioregions$site_species_matrix
        reference_k         <- clustgeo_results$parameters$optimal_k
        reference_alpha     <- clustgeo_results$parameters$optimal_alpha
        alpha_df_original   <- clustgeo_results$validation$alpha_evaluation
        env_data_final      <- get("env_data_final")

    # Retrieve coordinate and species data from the original analysis
        coords_df_original  <- get("coords_df")
        combined_species    <- get("combined_species_data")

    # Retrieve dissimilarity matrices from the primary analysis
        D0_ref <- clustgeo_results$dissimilarities$D0_ecological
        D1_ref <- clustgeo_results$dissimilarities$D1_geographical

# REPRODUCE THE ORIGINAL RNG SEQUENCE

    reproduce_original_sites <- function(coords_xy, k_final = 25) {
        set.seed(1999)

        # Replay the diagnostic k-means loop to advance the RNG state
            diagnostic_k_values <- seq(10, 100, by = 5)
            purrr::walk(diagnostic_k_values, function(k) {
                kmeans(coords_xy, centers = k, nstart = 50)
            })

        # Now run the final k-means (RNG state matches the original analysis)
            km_final <- kmeans(coords_xy, centers = k_final, nstart = 50)
        return(km_final)
    }

    # Verify reproduction: this should yield the same site assignments as Chunk 14
        km_reproduced <- reproduce_original_sites(coords_df_original[, 1:2], k_final = 25)
        reproduced_ids <- paste0("Site_", km_reproduced$cluster)

    # Build reference point-level bioregion labels using the reproduced assignments
        ref_site_to_region <- setNames(reference_clusters, rownames(site_species_ref))
        reference_point_labels <- ref_site_to_region[reproduced_ids]

    # Confirm: count of points with valid bioregion labels
        cat("Reference point-level labels: ",
            sum(!is.na(reference_point_labels)), "of",
            length(reference_point_labels), "points assigned\n")

# Build site-species matrix, extracts environmental data, computes
# dissimilarity matrices, and runs ClustGeo for a given configuration.

    run_pipeline <- function(coords_xy, species_data, k_sites, k_regions, alpha,
                             seed_val = NULL, replay_diagnostic = FALSE) {

        # Set RNG state
            if (!is.null(seed_val)) {
                if (replay_diagnostic) {
                    # Replay the diagnostic loop to match the original RNG sequence
                        set.seed(seed_val)
                        purrr::walk(seq(10, 100, by = 5), function(k) {
                            kmeans(coords_xy, centers = k, nstart = 50)
                        })
                } else {
                    set.seed(seed_val)
                }
            }

        # K-means site assignment
            km_result <- kmeans(coords_xy, centers = k_sites, nstart = 50)
            site_ids  <- paste0("Site_", km_result$cluster)

        # Construct site-species incidence matrix
            ssm <- species_data %>%
                sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
                dplyr::mutate(site_id = site_ids) %>%
                dplyr::group_by(site_id, species) %>%
                dplyr::summarise(presence = max(Presence), .groups = "drop") %>%
                tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = presence, values_fill = 0)

            ssm_df           <- as.data.frame(ssm)
            rownames(ssm_df) <- ssm_df$site_id
            ssm_mat          <- ssm_df %>% dplyr::select(-site_id) %>% as.matrix()

        # Site centroids
            centroids <- data.frame(x = coords_xy[, 1], y = coords_xy[, 2], site_id = site_ids) %>%
                dplyr::group_by(site_id) %>%
                dplyr::summarise(cx = mean(x), cy = mean(y), .groups = "drop")

        # Environmental extraction
            cent_sf  <- sf::st_as_sf(centroids, coords = c("cx", "cy"),
                                     crs = sf::st_crs(species_data))
            env_vals <- raster::extract(CovStack, cent_sf, buffer = 1000,
                                        fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
            rownames(env_vals) <- centroids$site_id

        # Subset to environmentally complete sites
            complete   <- complete.cases(env_vals)
            ssm_final  <- ssm_mat[complete, ]
            cent_final <- centroids[complete, ]

        # Guard against degenerate solutions
            if (nrow(ssm_final) < k_regions + 1) {
                return(list(clusters = rep(NA, nrow(ssm_final)), site_ids = rownames(ssm_final),
                            silhouette = NA, n_complete = sum(complete), km = km_result))
            }

        # Dissimilarity matrices
            D0 <- vegan::vegdist(ssm_final, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
            D1 <- as.dist(geodist::geodist(cent_final[, c("cx", "cy")],
                                           measure = "haversine") / 1000)

        # ClustGeo clustering
            tree     <- ClustGeo::hclustgeo(D0, D1, alpha = alpha)
            clusters <- cutree(tree, k = k_regions)

        # Silhouette score
            sil <- tryCatch(mean(cluster::silhouette(clusters, D0)[, 3]),
                            error = function(e) NA)

        list(clusters = clusters, site_ids = rownames(ssm_final), silhouette = sil,
             n_complete = sum(complete), km = km_result)
    }

    # Helper: compute point-level ARI against the reference
        compute_ari_vs_reference <- function(pipeline_result) {
            site_to_region <- setNames(pipeline_result$clusters, pipeline_result$site_ids)
            point_ids      <- paste0("Site_", pipeline_result$km$cluster)
            point_labels   <- site_to_region[point_ids]

            valid <- !is.na(point_labels) & !is.na(reference_point_labels)

            tryCatch(
                mclust::adjustedRandIndex(point_labels[valid], reference_point_labels[valid]),
                error = function(e) NA
            )
        }

# ==============================================================================
# AXIS 1: K-MEANS SEED STABILITY
# ==============================================================================
# Re-runs the full pipeline across 50 seeds with k_sites = 25, k = 3, α = 0.5.
# For each seed, the diagnostic loop is NOT replayed (only the reference uses
# that sequence), so each seed produces a independent site layout.

    seed_values <- c(42, 123, 314, 500, 777, 1066, 1453, 1776, 1848,
                     1917, 1945, 2001, 2020, 2024, 7, 13, 21, 37, 53,
                     89, 101, 199, 251, 307, 401, 509, 601, 701, 809,
                     907, 1009, 1103, 1201, 1301, 1409, 1511, 1607, 1709, 1801,
                     1901, 2003, 2111, 2203, 2309, 2411, 2503, 2609, 2707, 2801)

    cat("Running seed sensitivity across", length(seed_values), "seeds...\n")

    seed_results <- purrr::map_dfr(seed_values, function(s) {
        res     <- run_pipeline(coords_df_original[, 1:2], combined_species,
                                k_sites = 25, k_regions = 3, alpha = 0.5, seed_val = s)
        ari_val <- compute_ari_vs_reference(res)

        tibble::tibble(seed = s, ari = round(ari_val, 4), silhouette = round(res$silhouette, 4))
    })

    # Verify: reproduce the original with the replayed diagnostic RNG
        ref_check <- run_pipeline(coords_df_original[, 1:2], combined_species,
                                  k_sites = 25, k_regions = 3, alpha = 0.5,
                                  seed_val = 1999, replay_diagnostic = TRUE)
        ref_ari   <- compute_ari_vs_reference(ref_check)
        cat("Self-comparison ARI (should be 1.0):", round(ref_ari, 4), "\n")

    cat("\nSeed sensitivity summary (ARI vs. reference seed 1999):\n")
    cat("  Mean ARI:", round(mean(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
    cat("  SD ARI:",   round(sd(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
    cat("  Range ARI:", paste(round(range(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
                              collapse = " - "), "\n")
    cat("  Median ARI:", round(median(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
    cat("  Seeds with ARI >= 0.8:", sum(seed_results$ari >= 0.8, na.rm = TRUE),
        "of", nrow(seed_results), "\n")
    cat("  Mean Silhouette:", round(mean(seed_results$silhouette, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")

# AXIS 2: NUMBER OF SITES (K_SITES) SENSITIVITY
# Tests k_sites = 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 using the replayed RNG sequence (seed
# 1999 + diagnostic loop) so that k_sites = 25 correctly returns ARI = 1.0.

    k_sites_range <- c(15, 20, 25, 30, 35)

    k_sites_results <- purrr::map_dfr(k_sites_range, function(k_s) {
        res     <- run_pipeline(coords_df_original[, 1:2], combined_species,
                                k_sites = k_s, k_regions = 3, alpha = 0.5,
                                seed_val = 1999, replay_diagnostic = TRUE)
        ari_val <- compute_ari_vs_reference(res)

        tibble::tibble(k_sites = k_s, n_complete = res$n_complete,
                       silhouette = round(res$silhouette, 4),
                       ari_vs_ref = round(ari_val, 4))
    })

    cat("\nNumber of sites sensitivity:\n")
    print(k_sites_results)

# ==============================================================================
# BOUNDARY SITE IDENTIFICATION
# ==============================================================================
# For each seed, count how many sites change bioregion assignment relative to
# the reference. This distinguishes between "a few boundary sites flip" and
# "the entire partition reorganizes."

    # Rebuild the reference site-to-bioregion mapping at the occurrence-point level
    # (reference_point_labels already exists from the sensitivity chunk)

    # For each of the seeds, compute site-level and point-level diagnostics
        site_reassignment_diagnostics <- purrr::map_dfr(seed_values, function(s) {

            set.seed(s)
            km_temp    <- kmeans(coords_df_original[, 1:2], centers = 25, nstart = 50)
            point_ids  <- paste0("Site_", km_temp$cluster)

            # Build site-species matrix for this seed
                ssm_temp <- combined_species %>%
                    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
                    dplyr::mutate(site_id = point_ids) %>%
                    dplyr::group_by(site_id, species) %>%
                    dplyr::summarise(presence = max(Presence), .groups = "drop") %>%
                    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = presence, values_fill = 0)

                ssm_temp_df           <- as.data.frame(ssm_temp)
                rownames(ssm_temp_df) <- ssm_temp_df$site_id
                ssm_temp_mat          <- ssm_temp_df %>% dplyr::select(-site_id) %>% as.matrix()

            # Site centroids
                centroids_temp <- data.frame(
                    x = coords_df_original[, 1], y = coords_df_original[, 2],
                    site_id = point_ids
                ) %>%
                    dplyr::group_by(site_id) %>%
                    dplyr::summarise(cx = mean(x), cy = mean(y), .groups = "drop")

            # Environmental extraction
                cent_sf_temp <- sf::st_as_sf(centroids_temp, coords = c("cx", "cy"),
                                             crs = sf::st_crs(combined_species))
                env_temp     <- raster::extract(CovStack, cent_sf_temp, buffer = 1000,
                                                fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
                rownames(env_temp) <- centroids_temp$site_id

            # Subset to complete cases
                complete_temp  <- complete.cases(env_temp)
                ssm_final_temp <- ssm_temp_mat[complete_temp, ]
                cent_final_temp <- centroids_temp[complete_temp, ]

            # Guard against degenerate solutions
                if (nrow(ssm_final_temp) < 4) {
                    return(tibble::tibble(
                        seed = s, n_points_changed = NA,
                        pct_points_changed = NA, ari = NA
                    ))
                }

            # Dissimilarity and clustering
                D0_temp <- vegan::vegdist(ssm_final_temp, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
                D1_temp <- as.dist(geodist::geodist(
                    cent_final_temp[, c("cx", "cy")], measure = "haversine") / 1000)

                tree_temp     <- ClustGeo::hclustgeo(D0_temp, D1_temp, alpha = 0.5)
                clusters_temp <- cutree(tree_temp, k = 3)

            # Map back to occurrence-point level
                site_to_region_temp <- setNames(clusters_temp, rownames(ssm_final_temp))
                point_labels_temp   <- site_to_region_temp[point_ids]

            # Compare to reference at the point level
                valid <- !is.na(point_labels_temp) & !is.na(reference_point_labels)

            # ARI
                ari_val <- tryCatch(
                    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(point_labels_temp[valid],
                                              reference_point_labels[valid]),
                    error = function(e) NA
                )

            # To count "changed" points, we need to align cluster labels since
            # bioregion numbering is arbitrary across seeds. Use the Hungarian
            # algorithm via a confusion matrix to find the optimal label mapping.
                confusion <- table(
                    factor(point_labels_temp[valid], levels = 1:3),
                    factor(reference_point_labels[valid], levels = 1:3)
                )

            # Optimal assignment: map each seed-cluster to the reference-cluster
            # it most overlaps with (greedy assignment for 3x3 is exact)
                label_map <- purrr::map_int(1:3, function(row) {
                    which.max(confusion[row, ])
                })

            # Resolve conflicts: if two seed-clusters map to the same reference-cluster,
            # assign the smaller overlap to the next best
                if (length(unique(label_map)) < 3) {
                    # Fall back to clue::solve_LSAP for exact Hungarian solution
                        assignment <- clue::solve_LSAP(confusion, maximum = TRUE)
                        label_map  <- as.integer(assignment)
                }

            # Remap seed labels and count mismatches
                remapped_labels <- label_map[point_labels_temp[valid]]
                n_changed       <- sum(remapped_labels != reference_point_labels[valid])
                pct_changed     <- round(n_changed / sum(valid) * 100, 1)

            tibble::tibble(
                seed               = s,
                n_points_changed   = n_changed,
                pct_points_changed = pct_changed,
                ari                = round(ari_val, 4)
            )
        })

    cat("=== AXIS 1 SUPPLEMENT: SITE REASSIGNMENT DIAGNOSTICS ===\n\n")
    cat("Points changed per seed (vs. reference):\n")
    cat("  Mean:", round(mean(site_reassignment_diagnostics$n_points_changed, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
        "of 720 (",
        round(mean(site_reassignment_diagnostics$pct_points_changed, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "%)\n")
    cat("  Median:", round(median(site_reassignment_diagnostics$n_points_changed, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
    cat("  Range:", paste(range(site_reassignment_diagnostics$n_points_changed, na.rm = TRUE),
                          collapse = " - "), "\n\n")

    # Correlation between points changed and ARI
        ari_vs_changes_cor <- cor(
            site_reassignment_diagnostics$n_points_changed,
            site_reassignment_diagnostics$ari,
            use = "complete.obs"
        )
        cat("Correlation (points changed vs. ARI):", round(ari_vs_changes_cor, 3), "\n\n")

# ==============================================================================
# AXIS 1 SUPPLEMENT: CORE VS. BOUNDARY SITE CLASSIFICATION
# ==============================================================================
# For each occurrence point, track which bioregion it is assigned to across
# all seeds. Points consistently assigned to the same region (>= 80%) are
# "core"; the rest are "boundary."

    # Collect point-level bioregion assignments across all seeds
        all_seed_point_labels <- purrr::map(seed_values, function(s) {
            set.seed(s)
            km_temp   <- kmeans(coords_df_original[, 1:2], centers = 25, nstart = 50)
            point_ids <- paste0("Site_", km_temp$cluster)

            ssm_temp <- combined_species %>%
                sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
                dplyr::mutate(site_id = point_ids) %>%
                dplyr::group_by(site_id, species) %>%
                dplyr::summarise(presence = max(Presence), .groups = "drop") %>%
                tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = presence, values_fill = 0)

            ssm_temp_df           <- as.data.frame(ssm_temp)
            rownames(ssm_temp_df) <- ssm_temp_df$site_id
            ssm_temp_mat          <- ssm_temp_df %>% dplyr::select(-site_id) %>% as.matrix()

            centroids_temp <- data.frame(
                x = coords_df_original[, 1], y = coords_df_original[, 2],
                site_id = point_ids
            ) %>%
                dplyr::group_by(site_id) %>%
                dplyr::summarise(cx = mean(x), cy = mean(y), .groups = "drop")

            cent_sf_temp <- sf::st_as_sf(centroids_temp, coords = c("cx", "cy"),
                                         crs = sf::st_crs(combined_species))
            env_temp     <- raster::extract(CovStack, cent_sf_temp, buffer = 1000,
                                            fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
            rownames(env_temp) <- centroids_temp$site_id

            complete_temp   <- complete.cases(env_temp)
            ssm_final_temp  <- ssm_temp_mat[complete_temp, ]
            cent_final_temp <- centroids_temp[complete_temp, ]

            if (nrow(ssm_final_temp) < 4) return(rep(NA, nrow(coords_df_original)))

            D0_temp <- vegan::vegdist(ssm_final_temp, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
            D1_temp <- as.dist(geodist::geodist(
                cent_final_temp[, c("cx", "cy")], measure = "haversine") / 1000)

            tree_temp     <- ClustGeo::hclustgeo(D0_temp, D1_temp, alpha = 0.5)
            clusters_temp <- cutree(tree_temp, k = 3)

            # Map to point level
                site_to_region <- setNames(clusters_temp, rownames(ssm_final_temp))
                point_labels   <- site_to_region[point_ids]

            # Align labels to reference using confusion matrix
                valid <- !is.na(point_labels) & !is.na(reference_point_labels)
                if (sum(valid) < 10) return(rep(NA, nrow(coords_df_original)))

                confusion <- table(
                    factor(point_labels[valid], levels = 1:3),
                    factor(reference_point_labels[valid], levels = 1:3)
                )

                assignment <- clue::solve_LSAP(confusion, maximum = TRUE)
                label_map  <- as.integer(assignment)

            # Remap all point labels (including those not in 'valid')
                remapped <- rep(NA_integer_, length(point_labels))
                has_label <- !is.na(point_labels)
                remapped[has_label] <- label_map[point_labels[has_label]]

            return(remapped)
        })

    # Build a matrix: rows = points, columns = seeds
        label_matrix <- do.call(cbind, all_seed_point_labels)

    # For each point, compute the proportion of seeds assigning it to its
    # modal (most frequent) bioregion
        point_stability <- purrr::map_dfr(1:nrow(label_matrix), function(i) {
            labels_i <- label_matrix[i, ]
            labels_i <- labels_i[!is.na(labels_i)]

            if (length(labels_i) == 0) {
                return(tibble::tibble(
                    point_id = i, modal_region = NA,
                    modal_pct = NA, classification = "unassigned"
                ))
            }

            freq_table  <- table(labels_i)
            modal_region <- as.integer(names(freq_table)[which.max(freq_table)])
            modal_pct    <- round(max(freq_table) / length(labels_i) * 100, 1)

            tibble::tibble(
                point_id       = i,
                modal_region   = modal_region,
                modal_pct      = modal_pct,
                classification = dplyr::case_when(
                    modal_pct >= 80 ~ "Core",
                    modal_pct >= 50 ~ "Transitional",
                    TRUE            ~ "Boundary"
                )
            )
        })

    # Add spatial coordinates for mapping
        point_stability <- point_stability %>%
            dplyr::mutate(
                longitude = coords_df_original[, 1],
                latitude  = coords_df_original[, 2]
            )

    cat("Point stability classification:\n")
    point_stability %>%
        dplyr::count(classification) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) %>%
        purrr::pwalk(function(classification, n, pct) {
            cat("  ", classification, ":", n, "points (", pct, "%)\n")
        })
    cat("\n")

    # Breakdown by reference bioregion
        point_stability$ref_region <- reference_point_labels

        cat("Stability by reference bioregion:\n")
        point_stability %>%
            dplyr::filter(!is.na(ref_region)) %>%
            dplyr::group_by(ref_region) %>%
            dplyr::summarise(
                n_points   = dplyr::n(),
                mean_modal_pct = round(mean(modal_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
                n_core     = sum(classification == "Core"),
                n_trans    = sum(classification == "Transitional"),
                n_boundary = sum(classification == "Boundary"),
                .groups = "drop"
            ) %>%
            purrr::pwalk(function(ref_region, n_points, mean_modal_pct,
                                  n_core, n_trans, n_boundary) {
                cat("  Region", ref_region, "(n =", n_points, "):",
                    "mean stability =", mean_modal_pct, "%",
                    "| Core:", n_core, "| Transitional:", n_trans,
                    "| Boundary:", n_boundary, "\n")
            })

    # Create stability map
        point_stability_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
            point_stability,
            coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
            crs = sf::st_crs(combined_species)
        )

        stability_map <- ggplot() +
            geom_sf(data = Georgia_Boundary, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
            geom_sf(
                data = point_stability_sf,
                aes(color = modal_pct, shape = classification),
                size = 2, alpha = 0.8
            ) +
            scale_color_viridis_c(
                name = "Assignment\nStability (%)",
                option = "plasma",
                limits = c(0, 100)
            ) +
            scale_shape_manual(
                name = "Classification",
                values = c("Core" = 16, "Transitional" = 17, "Boundary" = 4)
            ) +
            theme_void() +
            theme(
                legend.position  = "right",
                panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
                plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
            )

        print(stability_map)

# ==============================================================================
# AXIS 2 SUPPLEMENT: K = 20 MULTI-SEED INVESTIGATION
# ==============================================================================
# Run k_sites = 20 across 20 independent seeds (without replaying the
# diagnostic loop) to determine whether a low ARI is specific to the
# replayed RNG state or structural to 20 sites.

    k20_investigation_seeds <- c(42, 123, 314, 500, 777, 1066, 1453, 1776,
                                 1848, 1917, 2001, 2020, 7, 13, 21, 37,
                                 53, 89, 101, 199)

    k20_results <- purrr::map_dfr(k20_investigation_seeds, function(s) {
        res <- run_pipeline(coords_df_original[, 1:2], combined_species,
                            k_sites = 20, k_regions = 3, alpha = 0.5,
                            seed_val = s, replay_diagnostic = FALSE)

        # Map clusters back to point level for ARI
            set.seed(s)
            km_temp    <- kmeans(coords_df_original[, 1:2], centers = 20, nstart = 50)
            point_ids  <- paste0("Site_", km_temp$cluster)

            site_to_region <- setNames(res$clusters, res$site_ids)
            point_labels   <- site_to_region[point_ids]

            valid   <- !is.na(point_labels) & !is.na(reference_point_labels)
            ari_val <- tryCatch(
                mclust::adjustedRandIndex(point_labels[valid], reference_point_labels[valid]),
                error = function(e) NA
            )

        # Check for degenerate cluster sizes
            sizes <- table(res$clusters)

        tibble::tibble(
            seed           = s,
            ari_vs_ref     = round(ari_val, 4),
            silhouette     = round(res$silhouette, 4),
            min_cluster    = min(sizes),
            max_cluster    = max(sizes),
            cv_cluster     = round(sd(sizes) / mean(sizes), 3)
        )
    })

    cat("\n=== AXIS 2 SUPPLEMENT: K = 20 ACROSS 20 SEEDS ===\n\n")
    cat("ARI vs. reference (k = 25):\n")
    cat("  Mean:", round(mean(k20_results$ari_vs_ref, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
    cat("  SD:",   round(sd(k20_results$ari_vs_ref, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
    cat("  Range:", paste(round(range(k20_results$ari_vs_ref, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
                          collapse = " - "), "\n")
    cat("  Seeds with ARI >= 0.8:",
        sum(k20_results$ari_vs_ref >= 0.8, na.rm = TRUE), "of", nrow(k20_results), "\n\n")

    cat("Cluster balance:\n")
    cat("  Mean min cluster size:", round(mean(k20_results$min_cluster), 1), "\n")
    cat("  Mean CV of cluster sizes:", round(mean(k20_results$cv_cluster), 3), "\n")

# ==============================================================================
# COMPILE SUPPLEMENTAL RESULTS
# ==============================================================================

    sensitivity_supplemental <- list(
        site_reassignment = list(
            diagnostics        = site_reassignment_diagnostics,
            ari_vs_changes_cor = ari_vs_changes_cor
        ),
        point_stability = list(
            classification = point_stability,
            spatial        = point_stability_sf,
            map            = stability_map
        ),
        k20_investigation = list(
            results = k20_results
        )
    )

    assign("sensitivity_supplemental", sensitivity_supplemental, envir = .GlobalEnv)

    cat("\n================================================================\n")
    cat("SUPPLEMENTAL SENSITIVITY DIAGNOSTICS COMPLETE\n")
    cat("================================================================\n")    
    
    
# ==============================================================================
# AXIS 3: NUMBER OF BIOREGIONS (K) SENSITIVITY
# ==============================================================================
# Uses the existing dissimilarity matrices (no k-means re-run), so results are
# exact and independent of RNG.

    k_region_range <- 2:5

    k_region_results <- purrr::map_dfr(k_region_range, function(k_r) {
        tree_temp     <- ClustGeo::hclustgeo(D0_ref, D1_ref, alpha = reference_alpha)
        clusters_temp <- cutree(tree_temp, k = k_r)

        sil <- tryCatch(mean(cluster::silhouette(clusters_temp, D0_ref)[, 3]),
                        error = function(e) NA)
        ch  <- tryCatch(fpc::cluster.stats(D0_ref, clusters_temp)$ch,
                        error = function(e) NA)
        ari_val <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(clusters_temp, reference_clusters)

        sizes   <- table(clusters_temp)
        cv_size <- sd(sizes) / mean(sizes)

        tibble::tibble(k_regions = k_r, silhouette = round(sil, 4),
                       calinski_harabasz = round(ch, 2), ari_vs_k3 = round(ari_val, 4),
                       min_cluster_size = min(sizes), cv_cluster_size = round(cv_size, 4))
    })

    cat("\nBioregion count sensitivity:\n")
    print(k_region_results)

# ==============================================================================
# AXIS 4: ALPHA NEIGHBORHOOD STABILITY
# ==============================================================================
# Pulls Q0/Q1 values from the ORIGINAL alpha_df computed in Chunk 14
# (which evaluated the full grid properly), then adds ARI for the
# neighborhood around the selected α.

    alpha_neighborhood <- seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.05)

    alpha_sensitivity <- purrr::map_dfr(alpha_neighborhood, function(a) {
        tree_temp     <- ClustGeo::hclustgeo(D0_ref, D1_ref, alpha = a)
        clusters_temp <- cutree(tree_temp, k = reference_k)

        sil     <- tryCatch(mean(cluster::silhouette(clusters_temp, D0_ref)[, 3]),
                            error = function(e) NA)
        ari_val <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(clusters_temp, reference_clusters)

        # Pull Q0_norm and Q1_norm from the original full-grid evaluation
        # (matches by nearest α in the original grid to avoid single-point normalization)
            closest_idx <- which.min(abs(alpha_df_original$alpha - a))
            q0n <- alpha_df_original$Q0_norm[closest_idx]
            q1n <- alpha_df_original$Q1_norm[closest_idx]

        tibble::tibble(alpha = a, Q0_norm = round(q0n, 4), Q1_norm = round(q1n, 4),
                       silhouette = round(sil, 4), ari_vs_ref = round(ari_val, 4))
    })

    cat("\nAlpha neighborhood sensitivity:\n")
    print(alpha_sensitivity)

    # Identify stable region
        stable_alpha_range <- alpha_sensitivity %>%
            dplyr::filter(ari_vs_ref >= 0.8)

        if (nrow(stable_alpha_range) > 0) {
            cat("Stable α range (ARI >= 0.8):",
                min(stable_alpha_range$alpha), "-",
                max(stable_alpha_range$alpha), "\n")
        } else {
            cat("No α values achieve ARI >= 0.8 against the reference.\n")
        }

# ==============================================================================
# AXIS 5: CUSTOM VEECH PROBABILISTIC CO-OCCURRENCE (REPLACES COOCCUR PACKAGE)
# ==============================================================================
# Implements Veech (2013) using the hypergeometric distribution.
# For species pair (j, k) across N sites:
#   P(J >= J_obs) = upper-tail hypergeometric (positive co-occurrence test)
#   P(J <= J_obs) = lower-tail hypergeometric (negative co-occurrence test)

    veech_cooccurrence <- function(site_species_mat, alpha_threshold = 0.05) {

        # Force binary incidence
            mat <- site_species_mat
            mat[mat > 0] <- 1

            N         <- nrow(mat)
            sp_names  <- colnames(mat)
            n_species <- ncol(mat)
            site_totals <- colSums(mat)

        # All unique species pairs
            pair_indices <- combn(n_species, 2)

        # Hypergeometric test for each pair
            purrr::map_dfr(1:ncol(pair_indices), function(idx) {
                i <- pair_indices[1, idx]
                j <- pair_indices[2, idx]

                n_i   <- site_totals[i]
                n_j   <- site_totals[j]
                J_obs <- sum(mat[, i] == 1 & mat[, j] == 1)
                J_exp <- (n_i * n_j) / N

                # Upper tail: observed co-occurrence >= J_obs (positive association)
                    p_positive <- phyper(J_obs - 1, n_i, N - n_i, n_j, lower.tail = FALSE)

                # Lower tail: observed co-occurrence <= J_obs (negative association)
                    p_negative <- phyper(J_obs, n_i, N - n_i, n_j, lower.tail = TRUE)

                association <- dplyr::case_when(
                    p_positive <= alpha_threshold ~ "positive",
                    p_negative <= alpha_threshold ~ "negative",
                    TRUE                         ~ "random"
                )

                tibble::tibble(
                    sp1_name = sp_names[i], sp2_name = sp_names[j],
                    sp1_sites = n_i, sp2_sites = n_j,
                    obs_cooccur = J_obs, exp_cooccur = round(J_exp, 2),
                    p_positive = round(p_positive, 6), p_negative = round(p_negative, 6),
                    association = association
                )
            })
    }

    # Run on reference matrix
        ssm_for_veech <- site_species_ref
        colnames(ssm_for_veech) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(ssm_for_veech))
        veech_custom_results <- veech_cooccurrence(ssm_for_veech, alpha_threshold = 0.05)

        veech_summary <- veech_custom_results %>%
            dplyr::count(association) %>%
            dplyr::mutate(proportion = round(n / sum(n), 3))

        cat("\nCustom Veech co-occurrence summary:\n")
        print(veech_summary)

    # Compare to archived cooccur results if available in the environment
        archived_veech <- tryCatch(get("complete_cooccurrence_analysis"), error = function(e) NULL)

        if (!is.null(archived_veech)) {
            archived_table <- archived_veech$veech_table

            veech_comparison <- veech_custom_results %>%
                dplyr::inner_join(
                    archived_table %>%
                        dplyr::select(sp1_name, sp2_name,
                                      p_gt_archived = p_gt, p_lt_archived = p_lt),
                    by = c("sp1_name", "sp2_name")
                ) %>%
                dplyr::mutate(
                    p_positive_diff = abs(p_positive - p_gt_archived),
                    p_negative_diff = abs(p_negative - p_lt_archived)
                )

            cat("Comparison with archived cooccur package results:\n")
            cat("  Mean |delta-p| (positive):",
                round(mean(veech_comparison$p_positive_diff, na.rm = TRUE), 6), "\n")
            cat("  Mean |delta-p| (negative):",
                round(mean(veech_comparison$p_negative_diff, na.rm = TRUE), 6), "\n")

            archived_assoc <- dplyr::case_when(
                veech_comparison$p_gt_archived <= 0.05 ~ "positive",
                veech_comparison$p_lt_archived <= 0.05 ~ "negative",
                TRUE                                   ~ "random"
            )
            cat("  Classification agreement:",
                round(mean(veech_comparison$association == archived_assoc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1), "%\n")
        } else {
            cat("Archived cooccur results not in environment; skipping comparison.\n")
        }

    # Co-occurrence stability across site configurations
        veech_by_k_sites <- purrr::map(k_sites_range, function(k_s) {
            # Use replayed RNG to match Axis 2
                res <- run_pipeline(coords_df_original[, 1:2], combined_species,
                                    k_sites = k_s, k_regions = 3, alpha = 0.5,
                                    seed_val = 1999, replay_diagnostic = TRUE)

            # Rebuild site-species matrix for this k_sites
                set.seed(1999)
                purrr::walk(seq(10, 100, by = 5), function(k) {
                    kmeans(coords_df_original[, 1:2], centers = k, nstart = 50)
                })
                km_temp <- kmeans(coords_df_original[, 1:2], centers = k_s, nstart = 50)
                ids     <- paste0("Site_", km_temp$cluster)

                ssm_temp <- combined_species %>%
                    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
                    dplyr::mutate(site_id = ids) %>%
                    dplyr::group_by(site_id, species) %>%
                    dplyr::summarise(presence = max(Presence), .groups = "drop") %>%
                    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = presence, values_fill = 0)

                ssm_temp_df           <- as.data.frame(ssm_temp)
                rownames(ssm_temp_df) <- ssm_temp_df$site_id
                ssm_temp_mat          <- ssm_temp_df %>% dplyr::select(-site_id) %>% as.matrix()
                colnames(ssm_temp_mat) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(ssm_temp_mat))

            veech_cooccurrence(ssm_temp_mat, alpha_threshold = 0.05) %>%
                dplyr::mutate(k_sites = k_s)
        })

    # Pair stability across site configurations
        significant_pair_stability <- purrr::map_dfr(veech_by_k_sites, ~ .x) %>%
            dplyr::filter(association != "random") %>%
            dplyr::group_by(sp1_name, sp2_name, association) %>%
            dplyr::summarise(
                n_configs_significant = dplyr::n(),
                mean_p = round(mean(ifelse(association == "positive", p_positive, p_negative)), 6),
                .groups = "drop"
            ) %>%
            dplyr::arrange(desc(n_configs_significant), mean_p)

        fully_stable <- significant_pair_stability %>%
            dplyr::filter(n_configs_significant == length(k_sites_range))

        cat("\nCo-occurrence pair stability across", length(k_sites_range), "site configurations:\n")
        if (nrow(fully_stable) > 0) {
            cat("Pairs significant in all configurations:\n")
            purrr::pwalk(
                list(fully_stable$sp1_name, fully_stable$sp2_name,
                     fully_stable$association, fully_stable$mean_p),
                function(s1, s2, assoc, mp) {
                    cat("  ", s1, "&", s2, "(", assoc, ", mean p =", mp, ")\n")
                }
            )
        } else {
            cat("  No pairs significant across all configurations.\n")
        }

        # Also report pairs significant in >= 3 of 5 configurations (majority-stable)
            majority_stable <- significant_pair_stability %>%
                dplyr::filter(n_configs_significant >= 3)

            cat("Pairs significant in >= 3 of", length(k_sites_range), "configurations:\n")
            if (nrow(majority_stable) > 0) {
                purrr::pwalk(
                    list(majority_stable$sp1_name, majority_stable$sp2_name,
                         majority_stable$association, majority_stable$n_configs_significant,
                         majority_stable$mean_p),
                    function(s1, s2, assoc, n_cfg, mp) {
                        cat("  ", s1, "&", s2, "(", assoc, ",", n_cfg, "/5 configs, mean p =", mp, ")\n")
                    }
                )
            } else {
                cat("  No pairs significant in a majority of configurations.\n")
            }

# ==============================================================================
# COMPILE RESULTS AND SUMMARY
# ==============================================================================

    sensitivity_results <- list(
        seed_stability = list(
            results   = seed_results,
            mean_ari  = round(mean(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
            sd_ari    = round(sd(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
            range_ari = round(range(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
            n_seeds   = length(seed_values),
            self_check_ari = round(ref_ari, 4)
        ),
        k_sites_sensitivity = list(results = k_sites_results),
        k_region_sensitivity = list(results = k_region_results),
        alpha_sensitivity = list(
            results = alpha_sensitivity,
            stable_range = if (nrow(stable_alpha_range) > 0) {
                c(min(stable_alpha_range$alpha), max(stable_alpha_range$alpha))
            } else { NA }
        ),
        cooccurrence_custom = list(
            veech_results      = veech_custom_results,
            veech_summary      = veech_summary,
            pair_stability     = significant_pair_stability,
            fully_stable_pairs = fully_stable,
            majority_stable    = majority_stable
        )
    )

    assign("sensitivity_analysis_results", sensitivity_results, envir = .GlobalEnv)

    cat("\n================================================================\n")
    cat("SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS SUMMARY FOR MANUSCRIPT\n")
    cat("================================================================\n\n")

    cat("1. K-MEANS SEED STABILITY (n =", length(seed_values), "seeds)\n")
    cat("   Self-check ARI (should be 1.0):", sensitivity_results$seed_stability$self_check_ari, "\n")
    cat("   Mean ARI vs. reference:", sensitivity_results$seed_stability$mean_ari, "\n")
    cat("   SD:", sensitivity_results$seed_stability$sd_ari, "\n")
    cat("   Range:", paste(sensitivity_results$seed_stability$range_ari, collapse = " - "), "\n")
    cat("   Seeds with ARI >= 0.8:", sum(seed_results$ari >= 0.8, na.rm = TRUE),
        "of", nrow(seed_results), "\n\n")

    cat("2. NUMBER OF SITES SENSITIVITY\n")
    purrr::pwalk(
        list(k_sites_results$k_sites, k_sites_results$silhouette, k_sites_results$ari_vs_ref),
        function(k, sil, ari) {
            cat("   k =", k, "| Silhouette =", sil, "| ARI vs. k=25:", ari, "\n")
        }
    )
    cat("\n")

    cat("3. NUMBER OF BIOREGIONS SENSITIVITY\n")
    purrr::pwalk(
        list(k_region_results$k_regions, k_region_results$silhouette,
             k_region_results$calinski_harabasz, k_region_results$ari_vs_k3),
        function(k, sil, ch, ari) {
            cat("   K =", k, "| Silhouette =", sil, "| CH =", ch, "| ARI vs. K=3:", ari, "\n")
        }
    )
    cat("\n")

    cat("4. ALPHA NEIGHBORHOOD STABILITY\n")
    cat("   Stable range (ARI >= 0.8):",
        paste(sensitivity_results$alpha_sensitivity$stable_range, collapse = " - "), "\n")
    ref_row <- alpha_sensitivity %>% dplyr::filter(alpha == reference_alpha)
    if (nrow(ref_row) > 0) {
        cat("   At alpha =", reference_alpha, ": Q0_norm =", ref_row$Q0_norm,
            "| Q1_norm =", ref_row$Q1_norm, "\n")
    }
    cat("\n")

    cat("5. CO-OCCURRENCE ROBUSTNESS (Custom Veech Implementation)\n")
    cat("   Total pairs evaluated:", nrow(veech_custom_results), "\n")
    purrr::pwalk(
        list(veech_summary$association, veech_summary$n, veech_summary$proportion),
        function(assoc, n_val, prop) {
            cat("   ", stringr::str_to_title(assoc), ":", n_val, "(", prop * 100, "%)\n")
        }
    )
    cat("   Pairs stable across all site configs:", nrow(fully_stable), "\n")
    cat("   Pairs stable in majority (>= 3/5):", nrow(majority_stable), "\n")
    
# ==============================================================================
# SUPPLEMENTAL SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
# ==============================================================================

    # Retrieve all sensitivity objects
        sensitivity_results     <- get("sensitivity_analysis_results")
        sensitivity_supplemental <- get("sensitivity_supplemental")
        clustgeo_results        <- get("clustgeo_bioregionalization")
        alpha_df_original       <- clustgeo_results$validation$alpha_evaluation

    # Reassemble key dataframes
        seed_results       <- sensitivity_results$seed_stability$results
        k_region_results   <- sensitivity_results$k_region_sensitivity$results
        alpha_sensitivity  <- sensitivity_results$alpha_sensitivity$results
        site_reassignment  <- sensitivity_supplemental$site_reassignment$diagnostics
        point_stability    <- sensitivity_supplemental$point_stability$classification
        point_stability_sf <- sensitivity_supplemental$point_stability$spatial
        stability_map      <- sensitivity_supplemental$point_stability$map

# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE S-A: SEED ARI DISTRIBUTION
# ==============================================================================
# Shows the full distribution of ARI values across 49 k-means initializations,
# illustrating the spread of clustering agreement with the reference solution.

    fig_sa <- ggplot(seed_results, aes(x = ari)) +
        geom_histogram(
            binwidth = 0.05,
            fill     = "#4169E1",
            color    = "white",
            alpha    = 0.8
        ) +
        geom_vline(
            xintercept = median(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE),
            linetype   = "dashed",
            color      = "red",
            linewidth  = 1
        ) +
        annotate(
            "text",
            x     = median(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.03,
            y     = Inf,
            vjust = 1.5,
            hjust = 0,
            label = paste0("Median = ",
                           round(median(seed_results$ari, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
            color = "red",
            size  = 3.5
        ) +
        labs(
            x = "Adjusted Rand Index (vs. Reference)",
            y = "Count"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
        )

    print(fig_sa)

# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE S-B: ARI VS. POINTS CHANGED SCATTERPLOT
# ==============================================================================
# Demonstrates the mechanistic relationship between the number of
# occurrence points reassigned between bioregions and the resulting ARI value.

    fig_sb <- ggplot(site_reassignment, aes(x = n_points_changed, y = ari)) +
        geom_point(
            size  = 2.5,
            alpha = 0.7,
            color = "#4169E1"
        ) +
        geom_smooth(
            method   = "lm",
            se       = TRUE,
            color    = "red",
            fill     = "red",
            alpha    = 0.15,
            linetype = "dashed"
        ) +
        annotate(
            "text",
            x     = max(site_reassignment$n_points_changed, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.7,
            y     = 0.95,
            label = paste0("r = ",
                           round(cor(site_reassignment$n_points_changed,
                                     site_reassignment$ari,
                                     use = "complete.obs"), 3)),
            size  = 4,
            color = "red"
        ) +
        labs(
            x = "Occurrence Points Reassigned (of 720)",
            y = "Adjusted Rand Index"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
        )

    print(fig_sb)

# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE S-C: ALPHA SENSITIVITY (Q-METRICS AND ARI)
# ==============================================================================
# Shows the normalized ecological and geographic quality metrics alongside ARI,
# identifying the stable plateau where the clustering solution is invariant to
# the mixing parameter choice.

    # Reshape alpha_sensitivity for dual plotting
        alpha_plot_data <- alpha_sensitivity %>%
            tidyr::pivot_longer(
                cols      = c(Q0_norm, Q1_norm, ari_vs_ref),
                names_to  = "metric",
                values_to = "value"
            ) %>%
            dplyr::mutate(
                metric_label = dplyr::case_when(
                    metric == "Q0_norm"    ~ "Ecological Quality (Q0)",
                    metric == "Q1_norm"    ~ "Geographic Quality (Q1)",
                    metric == "ari_vs_ref" ~ "ARI vs. Reference"
                ),
                metric_label = factor(metric_label,
                    levels = c("Ecological Quality (Q0)",
                               "Geographic Quality (Q1)",
                               "ARI vs. Reference"))
            )

    fig_sc <- ggplot(alpha_plot_data, aes(x = alpha, y = value, color = metric_label)) +
        geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
        geom_point(size = 2) +
        # Shade the stable ARI region
            annotate(
                "rect",
                xmin  = 0.25, xmax = 0.6,
                ymin  = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
                fill  = "grey80",
                alpha = 0.3
            ) +
        geom_vline(
            xintercept = 0.5,
            linetype   = "dotted",
            color      = "black",
            linewidth  = 0.8
        ) +
        annotate(
            "text",
            x     = 0.425, y = 0.05,
            label = "Stable Region\n(ARI >= 0.8)",
            size  = 3,
            color = "grey40"
        ) +
        scale_color_manual(
            values = c(
                "Ecological Quality (Q0)" = "#2E8B57",
                "Geographic Quality (Q1)" = "#4169E1",
                "ARI vs. Reference"       = "#DC143C"
            )
        ) +
        labs(
            x     = expression(paste("Mixing Parameter (", alpha, ")")),
            y     = "Score",
            color = NULL
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            legend.position  = "bottom",
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
        )

    print(fig_sc)

# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE S-D: K-REGION COMPARISON PANEL
# ==============================================================================
# Side-by-side silhouette and Calinski-Harabasz across K = 2-5, with K = 3
# highlighted as the selected value.

    fig_sd_sil <- ggplot(k_region_results, aes(x = k_regions, y = silhouette)) +
        geom_line(color = "grey50") +
        geom_point(
            aes(color = k_regions == 3),
            size = 4
        ) +
        scale_color_manual(
            values = c("FALSE" = "#4169E1", "TRUE" = "#DC143C"),
            guide  = "none"
        ) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
        labs(
            x = "Number of Bioregions (K)",
            y = "Mean Silhouette Width"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

    fig_sd_ch <- ggplot(k_region_results, aes(x = k_regions, y = calinski_harabasz)) +
        geom_line(color = "grey50") +
        geom_point(
            aes(color = k_regions == 3),
            size = 4
        ) +
        scale_color_manual(
            values = c("FALSE" = "#4169E1", "TRUE" = "#DC143C"),
            guide  = "none"
        ) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
        labs(
            x = "Number of Bioregions (K)",
            y = "Calinski-Harabasz Index"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

    fig_sd <- fig_sd_sil | fig_sd_ch

    print(fig_sd)

# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE S-E: STABILITY MAP (ALREADY GENERATED, REFINED HERE)
# ==============================================================================
# Refine the existing stability map with bioregion polygon overlay for context

    # Retrieve bioregion polygons if available
        bioregion_polygons <- tryCatch(get("bioregion_polygons"), error = function(e) NULL)

    if (!is.null(bioregion_polygons)) {
        fig_se <- ggplot() +
            geom_sf(
                data      = bioregion_polygons,
                aes(fill  = factor(bioregion)),
                alpha     = 0.15,
                color     = "grey40",
                linewidth = 1
            ) +
            geom_sf(
                data  = Georgia_Boundary,
                fill  = NA,
                color = "black",
                linewidth = 1.2
            ) +
            geom_sf(
                data = point_stability_sf,
                aes(color = modal_pct, shape = classification),
                size  = 2,
                alpha = 0.85
            ) +
            scale_fill_viridis_d(
                name   = "Bioregion",
                option = "turbo",
                begin  = 0.1,
                end    = 0.9,
                guide  = "none"
            ) +
            scale_color_viridis_c(
                name   = "Assignment\nStability (%)",
                option = "plasma",
                limits = c(50, 100)
            ) +
            scale_shape_manual(
                name   = "Classification",
                values = c("Core" = 16, "Transitional" = 17, "Boundary" = 4)
            ) +
            theme_void() +
            theme(
                legend.position  = "right",
                panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
                plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
            )
    } else {
        # Fall back to the original stability map without polygon overlay
            fig_se <- stability_map
    }

    print(fig_se)

# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE S-F: CO-OCCURRENCE PAIR STABILITY ACROSS SITE CONFIGURATIONS
# ==============================================================================
# Tile plot showing which species pairs were significantly co-occurring under
# each of the five site configurations (k = 15, 20, 25, 30, 35).

    # Rebuild the per-configuration significance data from Axis 5
        k_sites_range_cooc <- c(15, 20, 25, 30, 35)

        cooc_config_data <- purrr::map_dfr(k_sites_range_cooc, function(k_s) {
            # Replay the original RNG sequence for this k_sites value
                set.seed(1999)
                purrr::walk(seq(10, 100, by = 5), function(k) {
                    kmeans(coords_df_original[, 1:2], centers = k, nstart = 50)
                })
                km_temp <- kmeans(coords_df_original[, 1:2], centers = k_s, nstart = 50)
                ids     <- paste0("Site_", km_temp$cluster)

            # Build site-species matrix
                ssm_temp <- combined_species %>%
                    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
                    dplyr::mutate(site_id = ids) %>%
                    dplyr::group_by(site_id, species) %>%
                    dplyr::summarise(presence = max(Presence), .groups = "drop") %>%
                    tidyr::pivot_wider(
                        names_from   = species,
                        values_from  = presence,
                        values_fill  = 0
                    )

                ssm_temp_df           <- as.data.frame(ssm_temp)
                rownames(ssm_temp_df) <- ssm_temp_df$site_id
                ssm_temp_mat          <- ssm_temp_df %>%
                    dplyr::select(-site_id) %>%
                    as.matrix()
                colnames(ssm_temp_mat) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(ssm_temp_mat))

            # Run custom Veech co-occurrence
                veech_cooccurrence(ssm_temp_mat, alpha_threshold = 0.05) %>%
                    dplyr::filter(association == "positive") %>%
                    dplyr::mutate(
                        k_sites   = k_s,
                        pair_name = paste(sp1_name, "&\n", sp2_name)
                    )
        })

    # Identify all pairs that were significant in at least one configuration
        all_significant_pairs <- cooc_config_data %>%
            dplyr::distinct(sp1_name, sp2_name, pair_name)

    if (nrow(all_significant_pairs) > 0) {

        # Create a complete grid of pairs x configurations
            pair_config_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
                pair_name = unique(all_significant_pairs$pair_name),
                k_sites   = k_sites_range_cooc
            ) %>%
                dplyr::left_join(
                    cooc_config_data %>%
                        dplyr::select(pair_name, k_sites, p_positive) %>%
                        dplyr::mutate(significant = TRUE),
                    by = c("pair_name", "k_sites")
                ) %>%
                dplyr::mutate(
                    significant = tidyr::replace_na(significant, FALSE),
                    display     = ifelse(significant,
                                         paste0("p=", round(p_positive, 3)),
                                         "n.s.")
                )

        # Count configurations where each pair is significant (for ordering)
            pair_order <- pair_config_grid %>%
                dplyr::group_by(pair_name) %>%
                dplyr::summarise(n_sig = sum(significant), .groups = "drop") %>%
                dplyr::arrange(desc(n_sig)) %>%
                dplyr::pull(pair_name)

            pair_config_grid <- pair_config_grid %>%
                dplyr::mutate(pair_name = factor(pair_name, levels = pair_order))

        fig_sf <- ggplot(pair_config_grid, aes(
            x    = factor(k_sites),
            y    = pair_name,
            fill = significant
        )) +
            geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
            geom_text(
                aes(label = display),
                size  = 3,
                color = "black"
            ) +
            scale_fill_manual(
                values = c("TRUE" = "#4169E1", "FALSE" = "grey90"),
                labels = c("TRUE" = "Significant", "FALSE" = "Not Significant"),
                name   = NULL
            ) +
            labs(
                x = "Number of Sites (k)",
                y = NULL
            ) +
            theme_minimal() +
            theme(
                panel.grid       = element_blank(),
                legend.position  = "bottom",
                axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 9)
            )

        print(fig_sf)
    }

# ==============================================================================
# EXPORT ALL FIGURES FOR SUPPLEMENTAL ASSEMBLY
# ==============================================================================

    sensitivity_figures <- list(
        fig_sa_seed_ari_distribution  = fig_sa,
        fig_sb_ari_vs_reassignment    = fig_sb,
        fig_sc_alpha_sensitivity      = fig_sc,
        fig_sd_k_region_comparison    = fig_sd,
        fig_se_stability_map          = fig_se,
        fig_sf_cooccurrence_stability = if (exists("fig_sf")) fig_sf else NULL
    )

    assign("sensitivity_figures", sensitivity_figures, envir = .GlobalEnv)

    cat("All sensitivity figures generated and exported.\n")    
```

 CHUNK 21. TEMPORAL DISTRIBUTION OF COLLECTIONS FOR FIG1
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r FIGURE: TEMPORAL DISTRIBUTION OF TICK COLLECTIONS}
# ==============================================================================
# TEMPORAL DISTRIBUTION AND COLLECTION RECORDS SUMMARY
# ==============================================================================

    temporal_data <- Ticks_Raw_Georgia %>%
        filter(!is.na(Start_Date)) %>%
        mutate(
            Year  = lubridate::year(Start_Date),
            Month = lubridate::month(Start_Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
            Species_Full = paste(Genus, Species)
        ) %>%
        filter(Species_Full %in% species_list) %>%
        mutate(
            Lat_round = round(Latitude, 3),
            Lon_round = round(Longitude, 3)
        ) %>%
        distinct(Species_Full, Lat_round, Lon_round, Start_Date, .keep_all = TRUE)

    cat("Total collection records (all species):", nrow(temporal_data), "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: RECORDS PER SPECIES SUMMARY TABLE
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    records_summary <- temporal_data %>%
        group_by(Species_Full) %>%
        summarise(
            Records          = n(),
            Years_Sampled    = n_distinct(Year),
            First_Record     = min(Start_Date, na.rm = TRUE),
            Last_Record      = max(Start_Date, na.rm = TRUE),
            Most_Active_Month = names(which.max(table(Month))),
            .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        arrange(desc(Records))

    cat("\nCollection Records per Species:\n")
    print(records_summary, n = nrow(records_summary))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: PANEL A — ANNUAL COLLECTION EFFORT
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    annual_summary <- temporal_data %>%
        group_by(Year) %>%
        summarise(
            Total_Records  = n(),
            Species_Count  = n_distinct(Species_Full),
            .groups = "drop"
        )

    p_annual <- ggplot(annual_summary, aes(x = Year)) +
        geom_col(aes(y = Total_Records), fill = "#21908c", alpha = 0.8, width = 0.8) +
        geom_line(
            aes(y = Species_Count * (max(Total_Records) / max(Species_Count))),
            color = "#440154", linewidth = 1.2
        ) +
        geom_point(
            aes(y = Species_Count * (max(Total_Records) / max(Species_Count))),
            color = "#440154", size = 2.5
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(
            name = "Collection Records",
            sec.axis = sec_axis(
                trans = ~ . * (max(annual_summary$Species_Count) /
                               max(annual_summary$Total_Records)),
                name  = "Species Recorded"
            )
        ) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()) +
        labs(
            title    = "A. Annual Sampling Effort",
            subtitle = "Bars = collection records | Purple line = species richness",
            x        = "Year"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "#440154"),
            axis.text.y.right  = element_text(color = "#440154"),
            plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold")
        )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: PANEL B — MONTHLY PHENOLOGY HEATMAP
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    monthly_species <- temporal_data %>%
        group_by(Month, Species_Full) %>%
        summarise(Records = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
        complete(Month, Species_Full, fill = list(Records = 0)) %>%
        mutate(
            Species_Full = factor(
                Species_Full,
                levels = records_summary$Species_Full
            )
        )

    p_phenology <- ggplot(monthly_species,
                          aes(x = Month, y = Species_Full, fill = Records)) +
        geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
        geom_text(
            aes(label = ifelse(Records > 0, Records, "")),
            size = 2.8, color = "white", fontface = "bold"
        ) +
        scale_fill_viridis_c(
            option   = "viridis",
            name     = "Records",
            na.value = "grey95"
        ) +
        labs(
            title    = "B. Monthly Phenology of Collection Records",
            subtitle = "Species ordered by total records (descending)",
            x        = "Month",
            y        = NULL
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            axis.text.y     = element_text(face = "italic", size = 9),
            axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 9),
            panel.grid      = element_blank(),
            plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
            legend.position = "right"
        )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: PANEL C — RECORDS PER SPECIES (ORDERED BAR)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Extract genus levels in the same order they appear in Figure 2
        genus_levels <- presence_summary %>%
            mutate(genus = str_extract(Species, "^\\w+")) %>%
            dplyr::pull(genus) %>%
            unique()

    # Build a named colour vector using viridis discrete palette,
    # matching the scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis") call in Figure 2
        genus_colors <- setNames(
            scales::viridis_pal(option = "viridis")(length(genus_levels)),
            genus_levels
        )

    species_bar_data <- records_summary %>%
        mutate(
            Species_Full = factor(Species_Full, levels = rev(records_summary$Species_Full)),
            Genus        = str_extract(as.character(Species_Full), "^\\w+")
        )

    p_species <- ggplot(species_bar_data,
                        aes(y = Species_Full, x = Records, fill = Genus)) +
        geom_col(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
        scale_fill_manual(
            values = genus_colors,
            name   = "Genus"
        ) +
        labs(
            title    = "C. Collection Records per Species",
            subtitle = "Ordered by total records",
            x        = "Records",
            y        = NULL
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            axis.text.y     = element_text(face = "italic", size = 9),
            legend.position = "bottom",
            plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold")
        )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: PANEL D — SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF COLLECTION RECORDS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Convert temporal data to sf for mapping
        temporal_sf <- temporal_data %>%
            st_as_sf(coords = c("Lon_round", "Lat_round"), crs = 4326)

    # Build KDE surface weighted by record count per location
        location_counts <- temporal_data %>%
            group_by(Lon_round, Lat_round) %>%
            summarise(n_records = n(), .groups = "drop")

        location_expanded <- location_counts[
            rep(1:nrow(location_counts), location_counts$n_records), ]

        coords_map <- cbind(location_expanded$Lon_round, location_expanded$Lat_round)

        georgia_bbox <- st_bbox(Georgia_Boundary)

        kde_map <- MASS::kde2d(
            x    = coords_map[, 1],
            y    = coords_map[, 2],
            h    = c(bandwidth.nrd(coords_map[, 1]),
                     bandwidth.nrd(coords_map[, 2])),
            n    = c(500, 500),
            lims = c(georgia_bbox$xmin, georgia_bbox$xmax,
                     georgia_bbox$ymin, georgia_bbox$ymax)
        )

        kde_raster_map  <- raster::raster(kde_map)
        kde_cropped_map <- raster::mask(
            raster::crop(kde_raster_map, Georgia_Boundary),
            Georgia_Boundary
        )
        kde_df_map <- as.data.frame(raster::rasterToPoints(kde_cropped_map))
        colnames(kde_df_map) <- c("Longitude", "Latitude", "Density")

    p_map <- ggplot() +
        geom_sf(data = Georgia_Boundary, fill = "grey92", color = "black") +
        geom_tile(
            data = kde_df_map,
            aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, fill = Density),
            alpha = 0.75
        ) +
        scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = "Record\nDensity") +
        geom_sf(
            data  = temporal_sf,
            color = "black", size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5
        ) +
        labs(
            title    = "D. Spatial Distribution of Collection Records",
            subtitle = "Points = individual records | Surface = kernel density",
            x        = NULL,
            y        = NULL
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
            legend.position = "right"
        )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 7: COMBINE AND DISPLAY
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    temporal_figure <- (p_annual | p_phenology) / (p_species | p_map) +
        plot_annotation(
            title    = "Temporal and Spatial Structure of Georgia Tick Collection Data",
            subtitle = paste0(
                nrow(temporal_data), " collection records | ",
                n_distinct(temporal_data$Year), " years | ",
                n_distinct(temporal_data$Species_Full), " species"
            ),
            theme = theme(
                plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
                plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey40")
            )
        )

    print(temporal_figure)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 8: EXPORT FOR DOWNSTREAM USE
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    assign("temporal_data",    temporal_data,    envir = .GlobalEnv)
    assign("records_summary",  records_summary,  envir = .GlobalEnv)

    cat("\nSummary statistics:\n")
    cat("  Total records:", nrow(temporal_data), "\n")
    cat("  Date range:", format(min(temporal_data$Start_Date)), "to",
        format(max(temporal_data$Start_Date)), "\n")
    cat("  Years represented:", n_distinct(temporal_data$Year), "\n")
    cat("  Peak month overall:",
        names(which.max(table(temporal_data$Month))), "\n")
```

 CHUNK 22. VARIABLE IMPORTANCE PLOTS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r VARIABLE IMPORTANCE PLOTS}

  # Aggregate replicate-level importance data across all species
  importance_panel_data <- successful_ensemble_results %>%
      map_dfr(~ {
          .x$all_importance_data %>%
              mutate(
                  species_code    = .x$species_code,
                  species_display = .x$species_display
              )
      }) %>%
      # Compute mean and SD of relative influence per species per variable
      group_by(species_display, var) %>%
      summarise(
          mean_inf = mean(rel.inf, na.rm = TRUE),
          sd_inf   = sd(rel.inf,   na.rm = TRUE),
          .groups  = "drop"
      )
  
  # Order variables by overall mean importance (ascending, so highest plots at top)
  var_order <- importance_panel_data %>%
      group_by(var) %>%
      summarise(grand_mean = mean(mean_inf, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(grand_mean) %>%
      pull(var)
  
  importance_panel_data <- importance_panel_data %>%
      mutate(var = factor(var, levels = var_order))
  
  # Panel figure: horizontal dot-and-whisker plot with viridis colours
  importanceplot <- ggplot(importance_panel_data,
         aes(x = mean_inf, y = var, color = species_display)) +
      geom_pointrange(
          aes(xmin = mean_inf - sd_inf, xmax = mean_inf + sd_inf),
          position = position_dodge(width = 0.6),
          size     = 0.4
      ) +
      scale_color_viridis_d(option = "viridis") +
      labs(
          x        = "Mean Relative Influence (%)",
          y        = NULL,
          color    = "Species",
          title    = "Variable Importance Across Species",
          subtitle = "Mean ± SD across 100 ensemble replicates"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(
          legend.position    = "bottom",
          legend.text        = element_text(face = "italic"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
          panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
      )
  
    ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "variable_importance_plot.svg"),
           importanceplot, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

 CHUNK 23. VARIABLE PARTIAL DEPENDENCY PLOTS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r PARTIAL DEPENDENCY PLOTS}
  # Extract partial dependence data from a single replicate's gbm model
      extract_partial_dependence <- function(model, var_name, n_trees) {
          pd_grid <- plot.gbm(
              model, 
              i.var    = var_name, 
              n.trees  = n_trees, 
              return.grid = TRUE
          )
          
          # plot.gbm returns a data.frame with the variable and 'y' (logit-scale response)
          colnames(pd_grid) <- c("x_value", "y_response")
          pd_grid
      }
  
  # Build ensemble partial dependence for one species, one variable
      ensemble_partial_dependence <- function(species_code, var_name) {
          # Retrieve stored replicate results from global environment
              rep_results <- get(paste0(species_code, "_replicate_results"))
          
          # Extract partial dependence from each replicate
              pd_all <- map_dfr(seq_along(rep_results), function(i) {
                  rep_data <- rep_results[[i]]
                  
                  # Confirm the variable exists in this replicate's final model
                      model_vars <- rep_data$final_importance$var
                      if (!var_name %in% model_vars) return(NULL)
                  
                  pd <- extract_partial_dependence(
                      model    = rep_data$final_model,
                      var_name = var_name,
                      n_trees  = rep_data$optimal_trees
                  )
                  
                  pd %>% mutate(replicate = i)
              })
          
          if (nrow(pd_all) == 0) return(NULL)
          
          # Average across replicates at each x value
          # Bin x values to align across replicates with slightly different grids
              pd_all <- pd_all %>%
                  mutate(x_bin = round(x_value, 4)) %>%
                  group_by(x_bin) %>%
                  summarise(
                      mean_response = mean(y_response, na.rm = TRUE),
                      sd_response   = sd(y_response, na.rm = TRUE),
                      n_replicates  = n(),
                      .groups       = "drop"
                  ) %>%
                  rename(x_value = x_bin)
          
          pd_all
      }
  
  # Generate panel figure across all covariates for all species
      target_vars <- get(paste0(species_codes[1], "_ensemble_importance")) %>%
          filter(var != "landcover_class") %>%
          pull(var)
  
      pd_panel_data <- map_dfr(species_codes, function(sp) {
          sp_display <- ensemble_results[[sp]]$species_display
          
          map_dfr(target_vars, function(v) {
              pd <- ensemble_partial_dependence(sp, v)
              if (is.null(pd)) return(NULL)
              pd %>% mutate(
                  species_code    = sp,
                  species_display = sp_display,
                  variable        = v
              )
          })
      })
  
  # Faceted partial dependence panel
      ggplot(pd_panel_data, 
             aes(x = x_value, y = mean_response, color = species_display)) +
          geom_smooth(
          method = "loess",
          span   = 0.3,
          se     = FALSE,
          linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
          geom_ribbon(
              aes(ymin  = mean_response - sd_response,
                  ymax  = mean_response + sd_response,
                  fill  = species_display),
              alpha = 0.15,
              color = NA
          ) +
          facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
          labs(
              x        = "Covariate Value",
              y        = "Marginal Effect (logit scale)",
              color    = "Species",
              fill     = "Species",
              title    = "Ensemble Partial Dependence Plots",
              subtitle = "Mean ± SD across 100 replicates"
          ) +
          theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
          theme(
              legend.position = "bottom",
              legend.text     = element_text(face = "italic"),
              strip.text      = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
              panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
          )


```
